newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Merukh partner silent on Bre-X suit over Busang.
newsitem.headline: Merukh partner silent on Bre-X suit over Busang.

text.p: Australia's Golden Valley Mines NL president said on Monday it was too early to comment on how a report there was no economic gold deposit at Indonesia's Busang property would affect partner Jusuf Merukh's suit against Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd.

Golden Valley and Indonesian miner Merukh have a technical cooperation and financial agreement over the Busang property, which Bre-X had earlier estimated contained some 71 million ounces of gold reserves.
Merukh last year filed a C$2 billion lawsuit against Bre-X, claiming 40 percent of all three zones of the Busang field.
"At this stage, it's much too early to comment," Golden Valley president Warren Beckwith told Reuters in Jakarta. "We just got the news minutes ago."

In a stunning report to Bre-X released in Canada late on Sunday, consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said the Busang discovery was falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining".

Strathcona, which carried out an independent audit of the property, said it did not find an economic gold deposit in the southeast zone, the area claimed by Bre-X to contain about 71 million ounces of gold. Strathcona added that an economic deposit was unlikely to be found there.
Beckwith said Golden Valley and Merukh would study the effect of the announcement on the lawsuit, and if Bre-X had any assets.
"There are two issues. Firstly, the effect of the announcement on the case, and secondly, if the defendent had any assets...anything of value," he said.
Beckwith said attempts to hold meetings with Bre-X over their ownership dispute had been rejected by Bre-X.
